Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:10:1.hebrew: דלא מיחייבה - ללמד את בנה. דכתיב: ״ולמדתם את בניכם״, קרי ביה: ״ולמדתם״, לאקושינהו — דלא מיפקדא ללמוד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:10:1.english: That she is not obligated - To teach her son. As it is written: “And you shall teach your sons” — read into it: “And you shall study,” to compare them: that [since] she is not commanded to study, [she is not commanded to teach].

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:11:1.hebrew: אם היה בנו זריז - והאב רואה שיצליח ממנו, ואין לו סיפוק נכסים שילמדו שניהם — ילמוד בנו, והוא יטריח אחר מזונות ויספיקנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:11:1.english: If his son was diligent - And the father sees that he will be more successful than he, and he does not have sufficient means for both of them to study — his son should study, and he should toil for sustenance and provide for him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:12:1.hebrew: בי רבנן - בהמ"ד רחוק מן היישוב הוה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:12:1.english: The study hall - It was a study hall far from the settlement:

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:12:2.hebrew: לא ליתיב ליה אינש אושפיזא - לרב אחא, ועל כרחו ילין בבית המדרש, ומתוך חסידותו יעשה לו נס ויהרוג את המזיק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:12:2.english: Let no one give him lodging - To Rav Aḥa, and perforce he will spend the night in the study hall, and on account of his piety a miracle will be performed for him and he will kill the demon.

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:13:3.english: Like a serpent with seven heads - That it had seven skulls.

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:13:4.hebrew: כל כריעה דכרע - רב אחא מתפלל על אותו מזיק, נתר חד רישא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:13:4.english: Every bow that he bowed - Rav Aḥa was praying regarding that demon, [and] one head fell off.

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:13:5.english: You would have placed me in danger - You endangered me.

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:15:1.hebrew: הא לן הא להו - בני בבל היו הולכין וגורסין משניות התנאים בא"י. ומתוך שלומדים חוץ למקומם, אין צרכי הבית מוטלים עליו — נושא אשה, דהוה בלא הרהור, ואח"כ הולך ולומד תורה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:15:1.english: This is for us, that is for them - The people of Babylonia would go and study the mishnayot of the Tannaim in Eretz Yisrael. And since they study outside of their home place, the needs of the household are not cast upon him; [therefore,] he marries a wife so that he will be without [sinful] thoughts, and afterward goes and studies Torah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:15:2.hebrew: להו - לבני א"י הלומדים במקומם: אם נושא אשה, יהו צרכי הבית מוטלין עליו ויבטלוהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:15:2.english: For them - To the people of Eretz Yisrael, who study in their [own] place: if he marries a wife, the needs of the household will be cast upon him and will distract him [from his studies].

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:16:1.english: He saw him - Rav Huna [saw] Rav Hamnuna.

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:16:2.hebrew: דלא פריס סודר - כדרך הנשואין, שהיו רגילין לכסות ראשן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:16:2.english: That he did not drape a cloth [over his head] - In the manner of married men, who were accustomed to cover their heads.

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:1:1.hebrew: כל היכא - דלית ליה נכסי אלא ה' סלעים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:1:1.english: Anywhere - Where he has no property other than five selas:

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:2:1.hebrew: ככתובה בשטר דמיא - ובפדיון עצמו היה מחוייב קודם ששיעבד קרקעותיו, ויטרוף את הלקוחות. הילכך, בחמש בני חרי דאיכא, פריק לבריה; דאין זה אונאה, שהרי מצות בנו עליו יותר ממצותו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:2:1.english: Is considered as though it is written in a document - And he was obligated in his own redemption before he encumbered his land, and [the priest] may repossess from the purchasers. Therefore, with the five [sela'im of] unencumbered property that exist, he redeems his son; for this is not [considered] deception, since the mitzvah of his son is incumbent upon him more than his [own] mitzvah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:2:2.english: And the priest goes and repossesses - [From the] purchasers for his own redemption.

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:3:1.english: Is not considered as though written in a document - And [one] does not collect from encumbered [property].

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:8:1.hebrew: דכתיב ולמדתם - קרא אחרינא הוא: ״ולמדתם אותם ושמרתם לעשותם״ (דברים ה׳:א׳):
Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:8:1.english: As it is written: “And you shall study” - This is a different verse: “And you shall study them and observe to do them” (Deuteronomy 5:1).

Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:9:1.hebrew: דלא מיחייבה - ללמד את בנה. דכתיב: "ולמדתם את בניכם", קרי ביה "ולמדתם" לאקושינהו — דלא מיפקדא ללמוד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 29b:9:1.english: That she is not obligated - To teach her son. For it is written: “And you shall teach [velimadtem] your children,” [and] read into it: “And you shall study [ulmadtem],” to compare them — as she is not commanded to study.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 29b:15:1.hebrew: הא לן והא להו - פי' בקונטרס: בני בבל היו הולכין וגורסין משניות התנאים בא"י, ומתוך שלומדים חוץ למקומם, אין צרכי הבית מוטל עליהם; נושא אשה — דהוה ליה בלא הרהור — ואח"כ לומד תורה. "הא להו" — לבני א"י הלומדים במקומם: אם נושא אשה, יהו כל צרכי הבית מוטלין עליו ויבטלוהו. וקשה לר"ת: דמשמע דקאמר שמואל דנושא אשה תחלה כדי להיות בלא הרהור, ומוקי לה למילתיה בבני בבל — א"כ אכתי איכא הרהור, כיון שהולכים ללמוד חוץ למקומן! ועוד קשה: אחר שנשא אשה, היאך יצא חוץ למקומו ללמוד? והלא הוא צריך לחזור אחר מזונות אשתו ובניו! ובפ"ק דגיטין (דף ו:) אשכחן דשלח רבי אביתר: "בני אדם הבאים משם לכאן הם מקיימין בעצמן: 'ויתנו את הילד בזונה ואת הילדה מכרו ביין'" — פירוש: שצריכין בניו ובנותיו להתמשכן בעבור מזונותיהן — משמע שאין עושים יפה שהולכים ללמוד חוץ למקומן. על כן נראה לר"ת איפכא: דר' יוחנן, דאמר "ריחים בצוארו ויעסוק בתורה?!", לבני בבל דיבר — שאינו יכול להניח אשתו וילך וילמוד תורה, ועוד שהם עניים; ושמואל, דאמר "נושא אשה תחלה", לבני א"י אמר — שיכולים ללמוד במקומם, וגם הם עשירים, וטוב לו שישא אשה וילמוד תורה בטהרה. ומיהו, פעמים שגם בני א"י היו יוצאים חוץ למקומם לבבל ללמוד תורה, אלא רובם היו לומדים במקומם. ואין תימה אם שמואל שהיה מבני בבל דמורה לבני א"י — שהיו לפניו תלמידים מבני א"י שהיה מדבר להם; ור' יוחנן, אע"פ שהיה מא"י, היה מדבר לתלמידים שלפניו מבבל. וכן מצינו בפ"ק דשבת (דף ט.) גבי מאימתי התחלת אכילה: רב אמר "משיטול ידיו", ורבי חנינא אמר "משיתיר חגורו", ומפרש התם: "הא לן והא להו". וע"כ רבי חנינא, אע"ג שהיה מארץ ישראל, היה מדבר לתלמידים שלפניו מבבל, כדאמרי' התם: "הני חברין בבלאי, כיון דשרו המנייהו לא מטרחי להו", משמע דבני בבל היו רגילין בהתרת חגורה. ומיהו קשה מהא דאמר בפרק כיצד מברכין (ברכות דף מד.), דקאמר רב חסדא "על הארץ ועל פירותיה", ורבי יוחנן אמר "על הארץ ועל הפירות", ופריך עלה דרב חסדא: "אינהו אכלי ואנן מברכים?!", ומשני: "איפוך". ומאי קושיא? דלמא רב חסדא, שהיה מבבל, מדבר לתלמידים שהיו לפניו מא"י, ור' יוחנן לבני בבל, כמו בכל דוכתי! וי"ל: דקים להו דלא הוו באותה שעה תלמידי דרב חסדא מתלמידי א"י. ומיהו נראה לה"ר יצחק דמההיא דכיצד מברכין ל"ק מידי: דשאני ענין אכילה וברכות, דדין הוא לכל אדם שיברך לפי המנהג של מקום שהוא שם, אפי' לא היה מאותו מקום; ולהכי מתמה גמרא אליבא דרב חסדא שהיה מבבל: ולמה מברכין על פירותיה, דמשמע היינו פירות של א"י:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 29b:15:1.english: This is for us and that is for them - Rashi explains: The people of Babylonia would go and study the Mishnayot of the Tannaim in Eretz Yisrael, and since they studied away from home, household needs did not fall upon them; [therefore] one marries a woman so that he will be without [sinful] thoughts, and afterward studies Torah. "That is for them" — for the people of Eretz Yisrael, who study in their own locality: if one marries a woman, all household needs will fall upon him and disrupt his [studies]. And Rabbeinu Tam questions [this]: For it implies that Shmuel said that one marries a woman first in order to be without [sinful] thoughts, and [the Gemara] establishes his statement as referring to the people of Babylonia — if so, there are still [sinful] thoughts, since they go to study away from home! And furthermore, it is difficult: After he has married a woman, how could he leave his locality to study? Surely he must seek sustenance for his wife and children! And in the first chapter of Gittin (6b), we find that Rabbi Evyatar sent: "People who come from there [Babylonia] to here [Eretz Yisrael] fulfill in themselves: 'And they gave a boy for a harlot, and sold a girl for wine' (Joel 4:3)" — meaning that his sons and daughters must be pledged for their sustenance — which implies that they do not act properly by going to study away from home. Therefore, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam [to explain] the reverse: That Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said: "A millstone around his neck, and he shall engage in Torah study?!", spoke to the people of Babylonia — for one cannot leave his wife and go and study Torah, and furthermore they are poor; and Shmuel, who said: "He marries a woman first," spoke to the people of Eretz Yisrael — for they can study in their own locality, and they are also wealthy, and it is better for him to marry a woman and study Torah in purity. Nevertheless, at times the people of Eretz Yisrael would also go away from home to Babylonia to study Torah, but most of them studied in their own locality. And it is no wonder if Shmuel, who was of the people of Babylonia, instructed for the people of Eretz Yisrael — for there were students from Eretz Yisrael before him to whom he was speaking; and Rabbi Yoḥanan, even though he was from Eretz Yisrael, was speaking to the students before him who were from Babylonia. And so we find in the first chapter of Shabbat (9b) regarding from when the beginning of eating is: Rav said, "From when he washes his hands," and Rabbi Ḥanina said, "From when he loosens his belt," and [the Gemara] explains there: "This is for us and that is for them." And perforce Rabbi Ḥanina, even though he was from Eretz Yisrael, was speaking to the students before him who were from Babylonia, as we say there: "These Babylonian colleagues of ours, once they loosen their belts, one does not trouble them," which implies that the people of Babylonia were accustomed to loosening the belt. Nevertheless, there is a difficulty from that which is stated in the chapter Keitzad Mevarekhin (Berakhot 44a), where Rav Ḥisda said, "[One recites:] 'For the land and for its fruits,'" and Rabbi Yoḥanan said, "'For the land and for the fruits,'" and [the Gemara] raises an objection against Rav Ḥisda: "Do they eat [in Eretz Yisrael] and we recite the blessing [in Babylonia]?!", and answers: "Reverse [the opinions]." And what is the difficulty? Perhaps Rav Ḥisda, who was from Babylonia, was speaking to students who were before him from Eretz Yisrael, and Rabbi Yoḥanan to the people of Babylonia, as in every [other] place! And one can say: It was clear to them that at that time, Rav Ḥisda's students were not students from Eretz Yisrael. Nevertheless, it appears to the Rabbi, Rabbi Isaac, that from that [passage] of Keitzad Mevarekhin there is no difficulty at all: For matters of eating and blessings are different, as it is the law for every person that he should recite a blessing according to the custom of the place where he is, even if he was not from that place; and therefore the Gemara wonders according to Rav Ḥisda, who was from Babylonia: Why would they recite a blessing "for its fruits", which implies [the fruits] are the fruits of Eretz Yisrael.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 29b:2:1.hebrew: ואזיל כהן וטריף להו משעבדי - כלומר, בבני חרי פריק ליה לבריה; שאם היה פודה עצמו בבני חרי, לא היה פודה בנו ממשעבדי, דמיירי שנשתעבדו קודם שנולד הבן, ולכך מקדים פדיון בנו. ואין כאן אונאה ללקוחות, דמצות בנו עליו יותר ממצות גופו, כפ"ה. וק': דאדרבה, יש אונאה ללקוחות, דמצות גופו עדיף, ויאמרו: "פדה את עצמך בתחלה!" ואם יאמר: "אפדה את עצמי ממשעבדי", יאמרו: "אין נפרעין מנכסים משועבדים במקום בני חרי". ואפי' פדה בנו בכור מבני תרי, יאמרו לכהן: "הנחנו לך מקום לגבות ממנו, אותם חמש בני חורין". ולכך פירש ר"י, דמיירי כגון דאיכא חמש משועבדי' מיצחק, שעשאן אפותיקי לכהן בעבור יעקב בנו, ואח"כ מכרה, ושוב גדל יעקב והיה לו בן, ועמד הוא ובנו לפדות, ואין להם אלא ה' סלעים מבני חרי. ור' יהודה סבר: מלוה הכתובה בתורה ככתובה בשטר דמי, והיו לו אפותקאות בשטר לכהן קודם, ולכך גובה מהן, אע"פ שיש בני חרי ליעקב; לפי שמצותו על נכסי אביו יותר מעל נכסי עצמו, דחוב האב על נכסי האב ולא על נכסי הבן. ואינם יכולים לומר: "הנחנו לך מקום בנכסי יעקב", שאין עליו לשלם חוב של אביו, ומנכסיו אין לו כלום. וכן משמע הלשון דקתני: "שזה מצותו על אביו":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 29b:2:1.english: And the priest goes and repossesses the liened [property] - That is to say, [the father] redeems his son with the unliened property; for if he were to redeem himself with the unliened property, he would not be able to redeem his son from the liened property, since we are dealing with a case where [the properties] became liened before the son was born, and therefore he gives precedence to the redemption of his son. And there is no deceit of the purchasers here [by shifting the repossession onto their land], since the mitzvah of [redeeming] his son is upon him more than the mitzvah of [redeeming] his own person, according to the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi]. And [this is] difficult, for on the contrary, there is deceit of the purchasers! For the mitzvah of his own person takes precedence, and they will say: "Redeem yourself first!" And if he says, "I will redeem myself from the liened property," they will say, "One does not collect from liened property where there is unliened property." And even if he [already] redeemed his firstborn son from unliened property [bnei chori, printed as bnei teri], they will say to the priest: "We left you a place from which to collect — those five [sela'im of] unliened property." And therefore the Ri explained that we are dealing with a case where, for example, there are five [sela'im worth of] liened [land] from Yitzchak, who designated them as an apoteiki [specific security] to a priest for Yaakov his son, and afterward he sold it. And subsequently Yaakov grew up and had a son, and he and his son stood [in need] of redemption, and they have only five sela'im of unliened property. And Rabbi Yehuda maintains that a loan written in the Torah is like [a loan] written in a document, and the priest held prior designated mortgaged property [apoteikot] under a document; and therefore he collects from them [the purchasers of Yitzchak's land], even though Yaakov has unliened property — because his mitzvah is upon his father's property more than upon his own property, for the debt of the father is upon the property of the father and not upon the property of the son. And they [the purchasers] cannot say, "We left you a place [to collect] in Yaakov's property," because it is not his [Yaakov's] obligation to pay the debt of his father, and from his [Yitzchak's unliened] property he has nothing. And so too the wording implies, as [the baraita] teaches: "For this one, his mitzvah was upon his father."
